1.why: Four distinct logical relations (contrast, result, qualification, parallel); with the text hidden none is illegal.

2.why: Result, consequence, parallel and concession are all available relations; nothing in the option set rules any out.

3.why: Example, contrast, simultaneity and restatement are each viable without the preceding sentences.

4.why: Concession, restatement, simultaneity and correction are all legal relations blind.

5.why: Restatement, simultaneity, parallel and contrast are mutually exclusive but the option set gives no way to choose.

6.why: Same four-relation spread as other transition items; no option is self-defeating.

7.why: Only D contrasts the two studies' FINDINGS (memory link vs no link): A contrasts publication venue and samples, B reports one study only, C contrasts sample size, so none of them meets the stated goal whatever the notes say.

8.why: Result, comparison, concession and prior-time are all legal relations with the text withheld.

9.why: A and C describe the pre-existing cold-chain problem rather than why the innovation matters, so they cannot meet the stem's goal; B (what it does) and D (who it reaches) both remain legal, and D speaks to significance for a general reader.

10.why: Restatement, consequence, contrast and causal-consequence are all available; two result-type options do not cancel each other blind.

11.why: The goal is a single conclusion supported by ALL THREE studies; A, C and D each report one individual study's result, which by construction cannot be a conclusion drawn across three.

12.why: A ('can be expected to hold across most job types') and D ('beyond reasonable dispute for any job') are overgeneralizations a skeptic rejects, and B is a dismissal rather than a generalization; only C is hedged.

13.why: Contrast, result, parallel and intensification are each legal relations without the sentences.

14.why: Restatement, simultaneity, consequence and concession are all viable blind.

15.why: Example, parallel, contrast and result are all legal with the text hidden.

16.why: Sequence-closing, parallel, concession and consequence are all possible relations here.

17.why: Simultaneity/concession, consequence, contrast and restatement are all legal blind.

18.why: Intensifying addition, contrast, example and time-relation are all legal; the distinctive wording of A is not evidence.

19.why: Sequence, concession, parallel and summary are all viable without the passage.

20.why: Result, intensification, parallel and concession are all legal relations blind.

21.why: Simultaneity, restatement, correction and conditional-alternative are all available.

22.why: The goal is to emphasize a DIFFERENCE in distance between the two species; C and D each give one species' distance only and A asserts similarity, so only B places the two figures in opposition.

23.why: The goal requires both the self-rating and the measured performance; A gives only performance, C only the 8-hour group, D only study design, so none can express a disconnect.

24.why: Simultaneity, concession, consequence and summary are all legal relations with the text withheld.
